model_organism.citation: Growth arrest of PPP2R5C and PPP2R5D double knockout mice indicates a genetic interaction and conserved function for these PP2A B subunits (PMID: 35415460)
phenotypes: PPP2R5C single knockout mice are viable and survive normally
PPP2R5C and PPP2R5D double knockout (B56δγ-) mice arrest fetal development around embryonic day E12
Double knockout hearts have a single outflow vessel instead of both aorta and pulmonary artery (failure of outflow tract septation)
Strong genetic interaction between B56δ (PPP2R5D) and B56γ (PPP2R5C) required for heart development
model_organism.lethality: embryonic lethal (double knockout ~E12; single knockout viable)

model_organism.citation: LincR-PPP2R5C Promotes Th2 Cell Differentiation Through PPP2R5C/PP2A by Forming an RNA-DNA Triplex in Allergic Asthma (PMID: 38262392)
phenotypes: LincR-PPP2R5C KO mice show decreased Th2 differentiation
Reduced airway hyperresponsiveness in KO mice in OVA-induced asthma model
Reduced airway inflammatory responses in KO mice
LincR-PPP2R5C deficiency suppressed PP2A phosphatase activity and PPP2R5C expression, leading to decline in Th2 differentiation
CD4 conditional KO mice also showed decreased Th2 differentiation and reduced asthma phenotypes

model_organism.citation: LincR-PPP2R5C regulates the PP2A signaling pathway in the macrophage-myofibroblast transition in a mouse model of epidural fibrosis (PMID: 39729722)
phenotypes: LincR-PPP2R5C deficiency promoted M2-macrophage polarization
LincR-PPP2R5C deficiency increased macrophage-myofibroblast transition (MMT)
LincR-PPP2R5C deficiency aggravated epidural fibrosis in mouse laminectomy model
Enhanced MMT was abolished in mice with macrophage depletion
LincR-PPP2R5C modulated α-SMA expression in macrophages via PP2A signaling pathway

model_organism.citation: LincR-PPP2R5C regulates IL-1β ubiquitination in macrophages and promotes airway inflammation and emphysema in a murine model of COPD (PMID: 39018689)

LincR-PPP2R5C deficiency reduced pulmonary inflammation
Reduced IL-1β protein (but not mRNA) in macrophages of KO mice
LincR-PPP2R5C deficiency increased ubiquitinated IL-1β in macrophages via PP2A activity

model_organism.citation: LincR-PPP2R5C deficiency enhancing the fungicidal activity of neutrophils in pulmonary cryptococcosis is linked to the upregulation of IL-4 (PMID: 39287443)
phenotypes: LincR-PPP2R5C KO mice showed extended survival time after C. neoformans infection

Increased neutrophil numbers in lung tissue and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid of KO mice
LincR-PPP2R5C deficiency increased PP2A phosphorylation, enhancing fungicidal activity of neutrophils

model_organism.citation: LincR-PPP2R5C Deficiency Alleviates Airway Remodeling by Inhibiting Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition Through the PP2A/TGF-β1 Signaling Pathway in Chronic Experimental Allergic Asthma (PMID: 39155740)

Reduced epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in lung tissues of KO mice
LincR-PPP2R5C deficiency enhanced PP2A activity and inhibited TGF-β1 production in epithelial cells

model_organism.citation: A micropeptide TREMP encoded by lincR-PPP2R5C promotes Th2 cell differentiation by interacting with PYCR1 in allergic airway inflammation (PMID: 39025723)

Decreased glycolysis in Th2 cells from TREMP-/- mice
TREMP KO mice phenocopied PYCR1 KO mice in terms of reduced allergic airway inflammation

biological.citation: Pathogenic de novo variants in PPP2R5C cause a neurodevelopmental disorder within the Houge-Janssens syndrome spectrum. (PMID: 39978342)
biological.summary: De novo missense variants in PPP2R5C (encoding the PP2A regulatory B56γ subunit) cause a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delay, hypotonia, epilepsy, behavioral problems, and macrocephaly. Variants affect substrate binding, C-subunit binding, or both, and variably impair PP2A catalytic activity. A dominant-negative mechanism on substrate dephosphorylation is proposed as the pathogenic mechanism.

biological.citation: Growth arrest of PPP2R5C and PPP2R5D double knockout mice indicates a genetic interaction and conserved function for these PP2A B subunits. (PMID: 35415460)
biological.summary: CRISPR/Cas9n knockout of both B56δ (PPP2R5D) and B56γ (PPP2R5C) in mice causes fetal developmental arrest around embryonic day E12, with hearts displaying a single outflow vessel instead of separate aorta and pulmonary artery. Individual knockouts of B56γ alone are viable, indicating a strong genetic interaction between B56δ and B56γ specifically required for heart development. This suggests B56γ and B56δ form a functional subfamily within the B56 family.

biological.citation: Activation of ERK/IER3/PP2A-B56γ-positive feedback loop in lung adenocarcinoma by allelic deletion of B56γ gene. (PMID: 26986830)
biological.summary: Allelic deletion of PPP2R5C was found in 4 of 8 informative lung adenocarcinoma cases (50%), and PPP2R5C deletion or EGFR mutation together accounted for IER3/pERK overexpression in at least 67% of cases. PPP2R5C loss is proposed to activate an ERK/IER3/PP2A-B56γ positive feedback loop driving sustained ERK phosphorylation in adenocarcinoma. This is the first report of high-frequency PPP2R5C deletion in human carcinomas.

biological.citation: Differential gene expression profiles of PPP2R5C-siRNA-treated malignant T cells. (PMID: 23941244)
biological.summary: siRNA-mediated knockdown of PPP2R5C in Molt-4 and Jurkat T-cell leukemia lines significantly reduced proliferation without inducing apoptosis. Global gene expression profiling revealed 963 differentially expressed genes, with changes in TCR, Wnt, calcium, MAPK, and p53 signaling pathway genes; notably GSK-3β, ATM, and MDM2 were altered. This implicates PPP2R5C in multiple oncogenic signaling networks in T-cell malignancy.

biological.citation: Proliferation inhibition and apoptosis induction of imatinib-resistant chronic myeloid leukemia cells via PPP2R5C down-regulation. (PMID: 24004697)
biological.summary: PPP2R5C siRNA knockdown in imatinib-sensitive (K562, 32D-Bcr-Abl WT) and imatinib-resistant (K562R, 32D-Bcr-Abl T315I) CML cell lines and primary CML patient cells significantly reduced proliferation and induced apoptosis at 72 hours. Imatinib-resistant K562R cells showed significantly greater proliferation inhibition and apoptosis induction than sensitive K562 cells upon PPP2R5C knockdown. These results suggest PPP2R5C as a potential therapeutic target for imatinib-resistant CML.
biological.sample_size: 4 cell lines + primary CML patient cells

biological.citation: LincR-PPP2R5C Promotes Th2 Cell Differentiation Through PPP2R5C/PP2A by Forming an RNA-DNA Triplex in Allergic Asthma. (PMID: 38262392)
biological.summary: A lncRNA (LincR-PPP2R5C) forms an RNA-DNA triplex with the PPP2R5C promoter to enhance PPP2R5C expression and activate PP2A, promoting Th2 cell differentiation in a mouse asthma model. LincR-PPP2R5C deficiency suppressed PP2A phosphatase activity and reduced Th2 polarization, airway hyperresponsiveness, and inflammation. This establishes PPP2R5C/PP2A as a key axis in CD4+ T-cell Th2 differentiation downstream of a lncRNA regulatory mechanism.

biological.citation: Neural retina leucine-zipper regulates the expression of Ppp2r5c, the regulatory subunit of protein phosphatase 2A, in photoreceptor development. (PMID: 21078119)
biological.summary: The transcription factor neural retina leucine-zipper (Nrl) directly binds the Nrl-response element in the Ppp2r5c promoter, as confirmed by EMSA and chromatin immunoprecipitation, and enhances Ppp2r5c transcriptional activity. The affinity of Nrl binding to the Ppp2r5c promoter is dynamically regulated during mouse photoreceptor development. This identifies Ppp2r5c as a transcriptional target of Nrl during retinogenesis.

biological.citation: An Exploration of Osteosarcoma Metastasis Diagnostic Markers Based on Tumor-Associated Neutrophils. (PMID: 37272097)
biological.summary: PPP2R5C mRNA and protein were highly expressed in osteosarcoma cell lines U2-OS and MG63 compared to normal cell lines. siRNA-mediated knockdown of PPP2R5C reduced proliferation and migration while increasing apoptosis and p-AKT protein levels in these osteosarcoma cells. These findings suggest PPP2R5C influences osteosarcoma metastasis via the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.

biological.citation: ASHG 2019 - PgmNr 1273: Characterization of de novo variants in PPP2R5C expands the spectrum of PP2A-related neurodevelopmental disorders. (E. Brimble et al.)
biological.summary: Functional characterization of PPP2R5C missense variants in a HEK293 cell model showed significantly impaired co-precipitation of endogenous PP2A catalytic C and structural A subunits with GFP-tagged B56γ variants, and reduced PP2A catalytic activity on a phospho-peptide substrate. A recurrent variant p.E122K, affecting a residue that directly contacts the catalytic subunit, showed the most severe binding and activity defects. Six of seven individuals with these variants had macrocephaly, developmental/intellectual disabilities, and congenital hypotonia.

biological.citation: Prognostic Impact of PPP2R5C Gene Expression in Adult Acute Myeloid Leukemia Patients with Normal Cytogenetics. (PMID: 32158086)
biological.summary: PPP2R5C mRNA expression was significantly higher in peripheral blood of 50 de novo CN-AML patients compared to 20 healthy controls. High PPP2R5C expression correlated with unfavorable response to induction chemotherapy and significantly worse overall survival and progression-free survival. PPP2R5C overexpression was identified as an adverse prognostic factor in cytogenetically normal AML.
